secret_wo_version.description: Used together with secret_wo to trigger an update to the secret. Increment this value when an update to secret_wo is required. This field requires Terraform/OpenTofu 1.11+.

space_id.description: ID of the space the webhook is in

spacelift_named_webhook_secret_header.description: `spacelift_named_webhook_secret_header` represents secret key value combination used as a custom headerwhen delivering webhook requests. It depends on `spacelift_named_webhook` resource which should exist.

value_wo.description: Value for the header. The value is not stored in the state. Modify value_wo_version to trigger an update. This field requires Terraform/OpenTofu 1.11+.

value_wo_version.description: Used together with value_wo to trigger an update to the value of for the header. Increment this value when an update to value_wo is required. This field requires Terraform/OpenTofu 1.11+.

webhook_id.description: ID of the stack on which the environment variable is defined

spacelift_plugin.description: `spacelift_plugin` represents a Spacelift **plugin** - an instance of a plugin template that can be used to extend Spacelift functionality.

id.description: Immutable ID of the plugin

labels.description: Labels to apply to the plugin

parameters.description: Map of parameter ids to values.

plugin_template_id.description: ID of the plugin template to use

space_id.description: ID of the space the plugin is in

stack_label.description: Label to use when attaching the plugin to stacks

spacelift_plugin_template.description: `spacelift_plugin_template` represents a Spacelift **plugin template** - a reusable template that defines a plugin's behavior and can be instantiated multiple times as plugins.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the plugin template was created

id.description: Immutable ID of the plugin template

is_global.description: Whether this is a global (Spacelift-provided) plugin template

labels.description: Labels to apply to the plugin template

manifest.description: The plugin manifest defining the plugin's behavior

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the plugin template was last updated

spacelift_policy.description: `spacelift_policy` represents a Spacelift **policy** - a collection of customer-defined rules that are applied by Spacelift at one of the decision points within the application.

engine_type.description: Type of engine used to evaluate the policy. Possible values are `REGO_V0` and `REGO_V1`. Defaults to `REGO_V0`.

name.description: Name of the policy - should be unique in one account

space_id.description: ID (slug) of the space the policy is in

type.description: Type of the policy. Possible values are `ACCESS`, `APPROVAL`, `GIT_PUSH`, `INITIALIZATION`, `INTENT`, `LOGIN`, `PLAN`, `TASK`, `TRIGGER` and `NOTIFICATION`. Deprecated values are `STACK_ACCESS` (use `ACCESS` instead), `TASK_RUN` (use `TASK` instead), and `TERRAFORM_PLAN` (use `PLAN` instead).

spacelift_policy_attachment.description: `spacelift_policy_attachment` represents a relationship between a policy (`spacelift_policy`) and a stack (`spacelift_stack`) or module (`spacelift_module`). Each policy can only be attached to a stack/module once. `LOGIN` policies are the exception because they apply globally and not to individual stacks/modules. An attempt to attach one will fail.

module_id.description: ID of the module to attach the policy to

policy_id.description: ID of the policy to attach

stack_id.description: ID of the stack to attach the policy to

spacelift_repo.description:
`spacelift_repo` represents a Spacelift repo - a built-in version control system storing infrastructure code directly in Spacelift, without an external provider like GitHub or GitLab.

Repos have no branches: a stack always tracks the repo's latest commit.

created_at.description: Unix timestamp of when the repo was created

name.description: Name of the repo. The repo's ID (slug) is derived from the name when the repo is created, and does not change when the name changes.

space_id.description: ID (slug) of the space the repo is in. A repo cannot be moved between spaces.

stacks.description: IDs (slugs) of the stacks using this repo as their source code provider

updated_at.description: Unix timestamp of when the repo was last updated

vcs_checks.description: VCS checks configured for the repo. Possible values: `INDIVIDUAL`, `AGGREGATED`, `ALL`. Defaults to `INDIVIDUAL`.

spacelift_repo_file.description: `spacelift_repo_file` represents a single file in a [Spacelift repo](repo.md). Changing the contents, mode or encryption of the file commits a new revision, which triggers a tracked run on every stack the repo is attached to. Changing only the commit metadata does not.

author_email.description: Author email recorded on the commit

author_name.description: Author name recorded on the commit. Defaults to `Terraform`.

commit_message.description: Message recorded on the next commit that changes the file. Changing it on its own does not commit. Defaults to `Managed by Terraform`.

content.description: Contents of the file. Text only - binary files are not supported.

encrypt.description: Encrypt the file at rest. Spacelift never returns the contents of an encrypted file, so Terraform cannot detect changes made to it outside of Terraform. Defaults to `false`.

file_mode.description: Octal file permissions, for example `0755`. Defaults to `0644`.

path.description: Path of the file relative to the repo root, without a leading slash, for example `modules/vpc/main.tf`

repo_id.description: ID (slug) of the repo the file belongs to

revision_sha.description: SHA of the revision that last changed the file

size_bytes.description: Size of the file in bytes

spacelift_role.description:
`spacelift_role` represents a Spacelift **role** - a collection of permissions that can be assigned to IdP groups or API keys to control access to Spacelift resources and operations.

**Note:** you must have admin access to the `root` Space in order to create or mutate roles.

actions.description: List of actions (permissions) associated with the role. For example: `SPACE_READ`, `SPACE_WRITE`, `SPACE_ADMIN`, `RUN_TRIGGER`. All possible actions can be listed using the `spacelift_role_actions` data source.

description.description: Human-readable, free-form description of the role

id.description: Unique identifier (ULID) of the role. Example: `01K07523Q8B4TBF0YHQRF6J5MW`.

name.description: Human-readable, free-form name of the role

slug.description: URL-friendly unique identifier of the role, generated from the name. Example: `space-admin`.

spacelift_role_attachment.description: `spacelift_role_attachment` represents a Spacelift role attachment between an API key and a role within a specific space, an IdP Group Mapping and a role within a specific space, a stack and a role within a specific space, or a user and a role within a specific space. Exactly one of `api_key_id`, `idp_group_mapping_id`, `stack_id`, or `user_id` must be set.

api_key_id.description: ID of the API key (ULID format) to attach to the role. For example: `01F8Z5K4Y3D1G2H3J4K5L6M7N8`.

idp_group_mapping_id.description: ID of the IdP Group Mapping (ULID format) to attach to the role. For example: `01F8Z5K4Y3D1G2H3J4K5L6M7N8`.

role_id.description: ID of the role (ULID format) to attach to the API key, IdP Group, stack, or user. For example: `01F8Z5K4Y3D1G2H3J4K5L6M7N8`.

space_id.description: ID of the space where the role attachment should be created

stack_id.description: Slug of the Stack to attach to the role. For example: `my-stack`.

user_id.description: ID of the user (ULID format) to attach to the role. For example: `01F8Z5K4Y3D1G2H3J4K5L6M7N8`.

spacelift_run.description: `spacelift_run` allows programmatically triggering runs in response to arbitrary changes in the keepers section.

commit_sha.description: The commit SHA for which to trigger a run.

id.description: The ID of the triggered run.

keepers.description: Arbitrary map of values that, when changed, will trigger recreation of the resource.

proposed.description: Whether the run is a proposed run. Defaults to `false`.

stack_id.description: ID of the stack on which the run is to be triggered.

block.description: Custom runtime configuration to apply to this run, overriding the stack's defaults.

project_root.description: Project root is the optional directory relative to the workspace root containing the entrypoint to the Stack.

runner_image.description: Name of the Docker image used to process Runs

block.description: Environment variables for the run
Wait for the run to finish

continue_on_state.description: Continue on the specified states of a finished run. If not specified, the default is `[ 'finished' ]`. You can use following states: `applying`, `canceled`, `confirmed`, `destroying`, `discarded`, `failed`, `finished`, `initializing`, `pending_review`, `performing`, `planning`, `preparing_apply`, `preparing_replan`, `preparing`, `queued`, `ready`, `replan_requested`, `skipped`, `stopped`, `unconfirmed`.

continue_on_timeout.description: Continue if run timed out, i.e. did not reach any defined end state in time. Default: `false`

disabled.description: Whether waiting for a job is disabled or not. Default: `false`

spacelift_saved_filter.description: `spacelift_saved_filter` represents a Spacelift **filter** - a collection of customer-defined criteria that are applied by Spacelift at one of the decision points within the application.

created_by.description: Login of the user who created the saved filter

data.description: Data is the JSON representation of the filter data

id.description: Globally unique ID of the saved filter

is_public.description: Toggle whether the filter is public or not. If set to true, everyone can use it in the account.

type.description: Type describes the type of the filter. It is used to determine which view the filter is for. Possible values are `stacks`, `modules`, `auditTrailEntries`, `vcsIntegrations`, `blueprints`, `contexts`, `workerPools`, `webhooks`, `notifications`, `resources`, `policies`.

spacelift_scheduled_delete_stack.description: `spacelift_scheduled_delete_stack` represents a scheduling configuration for a Stack. It will trigger a stack deletion task at the given timestamp.

at.description: Timestamp (unix timestamp) at which time the scheduling should happen.

delete_resources.description: Indicates whether the resources of the stack should be deleted.

stack_id.description: ID of the stack for which to set up scheduling

spacelift_scheduled_run.description: `spacelift_scheduled_run` represents a scheduling configuration for a Stack. It will trigger a run on the given schedule or timestamp

at.description: Timestamp (unix timestamp) at which time the scheduled run should happen.

every.description: List of cron schedule expressions based on which the scheduled run should be triggered.

next_schedule.description: Timestamp (unix timestamp) of when the next run will be scheduled.

stack_id.description: ID of the stack for which to set up the scheduled run

timezone.description: Timezone in which the schedule is expressed. Defaults to `UTC`.

block.description: Customer provided runtime configuration for this scheduled run.

project_root.description: Project root is the optional directory relative to the workspace root containing the entrypoint to the Stack.

runner_image.description: Name of the Docker image used to process Runs

terraform_workflow_tool.description: Defines the tool that will be used to execute the workflow. This can be one of `OPEN_TOFU`, `TERRAFORM_FOSS` or `CUSTOM`. Defaults to `TERRAFORM_FOSS`.

block.description: Environment variables for the run

spacelift_scheduled_task.description: `spacelift_scheduled_task` represents a scheduling configuration for a Stack. It will trigger task on the given schedule or timestamp

at.description: Timestamp (unix timestamp) at which time the scheduled task should happen.

every.description: List of cron schedule expressions based on which the scheduled task should be triggered.

stack_id.description: ID of the stack for which to set up the scheduled task

timezone.description: Timezone in which the schedule is expressed. Defaults to `UTC`.

spacelift_security_email.description: `spacelift_security_email` represents an email address that receives notifications about security issues in Spacelift.

email.description: Email address to which the security notifications are sent

spacelift_space.description:
`spacelift_space` represents a Spacelift **space** - a collection of resources such as stacks, modules, policies, etc. Allows for more granular access control. Can have a parent space.

**Please note:** the `spacelift_space` resource requires root Admin permissions, and can only be used by administrative stacks in the root space, or using an API key or user session that has root space access.

inherit_entities.description: indication whether access to this space inherits read access to entities from the parent space. Defaults to `false`.

labels.description: list of labels describing a space

parent_space_id.description: immutable ID (slug) of parent space. Defaults to `root`.

spacelift_stack.description: `spacelift_stack` combines source code and configuration to create a runtime environment where resources are managed. In this way it's similar to a stack in AWS CloudFormation, or a project on generic CI/CD platforms.

additional_project_globs.description: Project globs is an optional list of paths to track changes of in addition to the project root.

administrative.description: Indicates whether this stack can manage others. Defaults to `false`. This field will be removed in a future version. Use `spacelift_role_attachment` resource to manage stack permissions.

allow_run_promotion.description: Indicates whether a proposed run can be promoted to a tracked run. Defaults to `true`.

autodeploy.description: Indicates whether changes to this stack can be automatically deployed. Defaults to `false`.

autoretry.description: Indicates whether obsolete proposed changes should automatically be retried. Defaults to `false`.

aws_assume_role_policy_statement.description: AWS IAM assume role policy statement setting up trust relationship

branch.description: Git branch to apply changes to

enable_local_preview.description: Indicates whether local preview runs can be triggered on this Stack. Defaults to `false`.

enable_sensitive_outputs_upload.description: Indicates whether sensitive outputs created by this stack can be uploaded to Spacelift to be used by Stack Dependency references. Triggered only when corresponding option is enabled on the Worker Pool used by the Stack as well. Defaults to `true`.

enable_well_known_secret_masking.description: Indicates whether well-known secret masking is enabled.

git_sparse_checkout_paths.description: Git sparse checkout paths is an optional list of paths to use for sparse checkout. If not set, the entire repository will be checked out.

github_action_deploy.description: Use `allow_run_promotion` instead. Indicates whether GitHub users can promote proposed runs to tracked runs from the Checks API. This is called allow run promotion in the UI. Defaults to `true`.

import_state.description: State file to upload when creating a new stack

import_state_file.description: Path to the state file to upload when creating a new stack

manage_state.description: Determines if Spacelift should manage state for this stack. Defaults to `true`.

name.description: Name of the stack - should be unique in one account

prevent_changes_when_locked.description: If true, Terraform will fail when the stack is locked and the plan would modify or destroy this resource. Defaults to `false`. Note: destroy errors are (currently) raised during the apply, not planning.

project_root.description: Project root is the optional directory relative to the workspace root containing the entrypoint to the Stack.

protect_from_deletion.description: Protect this stack from accidental deletion. If set, attempts to delete this stack will fail. Defaults to `false`.

repository.description: Name of the repository, without the owner part

runner_image.description: Name of the Docker image used to process Runs

slug.description: Allows setting the custom ID (slug) for the stack

space_id.description: ID (slug) of the space the stack is in. Defaults to `legacy` if it exists, otherwise `root`.

terraform_external_state_access.description: Indicates whether you can access the Stack state file from other stacks or outside of Spacelift. Defaults to `false`.

terraform_smart_sanitization.description: Indicates whether runs on this will use terraform's sensitive value system to sanitize the outputs of Terraform state and plans in spacelift instead of sanitizing all fields. Note: Requires the terraform version to be v1.0.1 or above. Defaults to `false`.

terraform_workflow_tool.description: Defines the tool that will be used to execute the workflow. This can be one of `OPEN_TOFU`, `TERRAFORM_FOSS` or `CUSTOM`. Defaults to `TERRAFORM_FOSS`.

worker_pool_id.description: ID of the worker pool to use. NOTE: worker_pool_id is required when using a self-hosted instance of Spacelift.

block.description: Ansible-specific configuration. Presence means this Stack is an Ansible Stack.
Azure DevOps VCS settings

id.description: The ID of the Azure Devops integration. If not specified, the default integration will be used.

is_default.description: Indicates whether this is the default Azure DevOps integration

project.description: The name of the Azure DevOps project

block.description: Bitbucket Cloud VCS settings

id.description: The ID of the Bitbucket Cloud integration. If not specified, the default integration will be used.

is_default.description: Indicates whether this is the default Bitbucket Cloud integration

namespace.description: The Bitbucket project containing the repository

block.description: Bitbucket Datacenter VCS settings

id.description: The ID of the Bitbucket Datacenter integration. If not specified, the default integration will be used.

is_default.description: Indicates whether this is the default Bitbucket Datacenter integration

namespace.description: The Bitbucket project containing the repository

block.description: CloudFormation-specific configuration. Presence means this Stack is a CloudFormation Stack.

entry_template_file.description: Template file `cloudformation package` will be called on

template_bucket.description: S3 bucket to save CloudFormation templates to

block.description: VCS settings for [GitHub custom application](https://docs.spacelift.io/integrations/source-control/github#setting-up-the-custom-application)

id.description: The ID of the GitHub Enterprise integration. If not specified, the default integration will be used.

is_default.description: Indicates whether this is the default GitHub Enterprise integration

namespace.description: The GitHub organization / user the repository belongs to

block.description: GitLab VCS settings

id.description: The ID of the Gitlab integration. If not specified, the default integration will be used.

is_default.description: Indicates whether this is the default GitLab integration

namespace.description: The GitLab namespace containing the repository

block.description: Kubernetes-specific configuration. Presence means this Stack is a Kubernetes Stack.

kubernetes_workflow_tool.description: Defines the tool that will be used to execute the workflow. This can be one of `KUBERNETES` or `CUSTOM`. Defaults to `KUBERNETES`.

namespace.description: Namespace of the Kubernetes cluster to run commands on. Leave empty for multi-namespace Stacks.

block.description: OpenTofu-specific configuration. Presence means this Stack is a native OpenTofu Stack.

external_state_access.description: Indicates whether you can access the Stack state file from other stacks or outside of Spacelift. Defaults to `false`.

use_smart_sanitization.description: Indicates whether runs on this will use OpenTofu's sensitive value system to sanitize the outputs of state and plans in Spacelift instead of sanitizing all fields. Defaults to `true`.

workflow_tool.description: Defines the tool that will be used to execute the workflow. This can be one of `OPENTOFU` or `CUSTOM`. Defaults to `OPENTOFU`.

block.description: Logging configuration for OpenTofu commands.

concise.description: Enables the -concise flag for OpenTofu plan/apply/refresh commands. Requires OpenTofu 1.7+. Defaults to `true`.

block.description: Use the installed account-level Origin integration. The repository and branch are configured by the corresponding top-level attributes.
Pulumi-specific configuration. Presence means this Stack is a Pulumi Stack.

login_url.description: State backend to log into on Run initialize.

stack_name.description: Pulumi stack name to use with the state backend.

block.description: One-way VCS integration using a raw Git repository link

namespace.description: User-friendly namespace for the repository, this is for cosmetic purposes only

url.description: HTTPS URL of the Git repository

block.description: Take the source from a Spacelift repo. The block takes no settings: `repository` is the repo's ID (slug), and `branch` must be `main` - Spacelift Repos have no branches, and the stack always tracks the latest commit.
Terragrunt-specific configuration. Presence means this Stack is an Terragrunt Stack.

prefix_resource_names_with_module_name.description: Controls whether resource and output names are prefixed with the module path. Has no effect when use_run_all is enabled (always prefixes in that case).

skip_replan.description: If set to true, the apply phase will reuse the plan from the planning phase instead of re-planning. Applies to both run-all and non-run-all stacks. Warning: this means any `mocked_outputs` referenced during planning will be applied as-is — do not enable this together with `mocked_outputs` unless you fully understand the implications, your apply may execute against mocked values rather than real ones.

skip_replan_when_run_all.description: When using Run All, skip the second planning phase during the apply stage. This is an experimental feature. Runs with Run All disabled reuse the plan by default. Warning: this means any `mocked_outputs` referenced during planning will be applied as-is — do not enable this together with `mocked_outputs` unless you fully understand the implications, your apply may execute against mocked values rather than real ones.

terraform_version.description: The Terraform version. Must not be provided when tool is set to MANUALLY_PROVISIONED. Defaults to the latest available OpenTofu/Terraform version.

terragrunt_version.description: The Terragrunt version. Defaults to the latest Terragrunt version.

tool.description: The IaC tool used by Terragrunt. Valid values are OPEN_TOFU, TERRAFORM_FOSS or MANUALLY_PROVISIONED. Defaults to TERRAFORM_FOSS if not specified.

use_run_all.description: Whether to use `terragrunt run-all` instead of `terragrunt`.

use_smart_sanitization.description: Indicates whether runs on this will use Terraform's sensitive value system to sanitize the outputs of Terraform state and plans in spacelift instead of sanitizing all fields.

use_state_management.description: Determines if Spacelift should manage state for this Terragrunt stack. Takes precedence over `manage_state`. Defaults to `false`.

spacelift_stack_activator.description: `spacelift_stack_activator` is used to to enable/disable Spacelift Stack.

stack_id.description: ID of the stack to enable/disable

spacelift_stack_aws_role.description:
~> **Note:** `spacelift_stack_aws_role` is deprecated. Please use `spacelift_aws_role` instead. The functionality is identical.

**NOTE:** while this resource continues to work, we have replaced it with the `spacelift_aws_integration` resource. The new resource allows integrations to be shared by multiple stacks/modules and also supports separate read vs write roles. Please use the `spacelift_aws_integration` resource instead.

`spacelift_stack_aws_role` represents [cross-account IAM role delegation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/tutorial_cross-account-with-roles.html) between the Spacelift worker and an individual stack or module. If this is set, Spacelift will use AWS STS to assume the supplied IAM role and put its temporary credentials in the runtime environment.

If you use private workers, you can also assume IAM role on the worker side using your own AWS credentials (e.g. from EC2 instance profile).

Note: when assuming credentials for **shared worker**, Spacelift will use `$accountName@$stackID` or `$accountName@$moduleID` as [external ID](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_create_for-user_externalid.html) and `$runID@$stackID@$accountName` truncated to 64 characters as [session ID](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/STS/latest/APIReference/API_AssumeRole).

duration_seconds.description: AWS IAM role session duration in seconds

external_id.description: Custom external ID (works only for private workers).

generate_credentials_in_worker.description: Generate AWS credentials in the private worker. Defaults to `false`.

module_id.description: ID of the module which assumes the AWS IAM role

region.description: AWS region to select a regional AWS STS endpoint.

role_arn.description: ARN of the AWS IAM role to attach

stack_id.description: ID of the stack which assumes the AWS IAM role

spacelift_stack_dependency.description: `spacelift_stack_dependency` represents a Spacelift **stack dependency** - a dependency between two stacks. When one stack depends on another, the tracked runs of the stack will not start until the dependent stack is successfully finished. Additionally, changes to the dependency will trigger the dependent.

depends_on_stack_id.description: immutable ID (slug) of stack to depend on.

stack_id.description: immutable ID (slug) of stack which has a dependency.

trigger_always.description: Whether the dependent stack should be triggered on every successful run of the stack it depends on, even if none of the dependency outputs have changed. Defaults to `false`.

spacelift_stack_dependency_reference.description: `spacelift_stack_dependency_reference` represents a Spacelift **stack dependency reference** - a reference matches a stack's output to another stack's input. It is similar to an environment variable (`spacelift_environment_variable`), except that value is provided by another stack's output.

input_name.description: Name of the input of the stack dependency reference

output_name.description: Name of the output of stack to depend on

trigger_always.description: Whether the dependents should be triggered even if the value of the reference did not change.

spacelift_stack_destructor.description: `spacelift_stack_destructor` is used to destroy the resources of a Stack before deleting it. `depends_on` should be used to make sure that all necessary resources (environment variables, roles, integrations, etc.) are still in place when the destruction run is executed. **Note:** Destroying this resource will delete the resources in the stack. If this resource needs to be deleted and the resources in the stacks are to be preserved, ensure that the `deactivated` attribute is set to `true`.

deactivated.description: If set to true, destruction won't delete the resources (e.g. AWS/Azure/GCP infrastructure) managed by the stack

discard_runs.description: If set to true, destruction will also discard all runs on the stack that are eligible for discarding (e.g. not in progress runs)

stack_id.description: ID of the stack to delete and destroy on destruction

spacelift_stack_gcp_service_account.description:
~> **Note:** `spacelift_stack_gcp_service_account` is deprecated. Please use `spacelift_gcp_service_account` instead. The functionality is identical.

`spacelift_stack_gcp_service_account` represents a Google Cloud Platform service account that's linked to a particular Stack or Module. These accounts are created by Spacelift on per-stack basis, and can be added as members to as many organizations and projects as needed. During a Run or a Task, temporary credentials for those service accounts are injected into the environment, which allows credential-less GCP Terraform provider setup.

module_id.description: ID of the module which uses GCP service account credentials

service_account_email.description: Email address of the GCP service account dedicated for this stack

stack_id.description: ID of the stack which uses GCP service account credentials

token_scopes.description: List of scopes that will be requested when generating temporary GCP service account credentials

init.description: Whether to initialize the stack or not. Default: `true`

keepers.description: Arbitrary map of values that, when changed, will trigger recreation of the resource.

stack_id.description: ID of the stack for which to run the task

block.description: Wait for the run to finish

continue_on_state.description: Continue on the specified states of a finished run. If not specified, the default is `[ 'finished' ]`. You can use following states: `applying`, `canceled`, `confirmed`, `destroying`, `discarded`, `failed`, `finished`, `initializing`, `pending_review`, `performing`, `planning`, `preparing_apply`, `preparing_replan`, `preparing`, `queued`, `ready`, `replan_requested`, `skipped`, `stopped`, `unconfirmed`.

continue_on_timeout.description: Continue if task timed out, i.e. did not reach any defined end state in time. Default: `false`

disabled.description: Whether waiting for the task is disabled or not. Default: `false`

spacelift_template.description: `spacelift_template` represents a Spacelift template (versioned blueprint), which is a collection of blueprint versions that can be used to create stacks.

created_at.description: Unix timestamp when the template was created

space.description: ID of the space the template is in

updated_at.description: Unix timestamp when the template was last updated

spacelift_template_deployment.description: `spacelift_template_deployment` deploys a Spacelift template, creating and managing the stacks defined in the template.

created_at.description: Unix timestamp when the deployment was created

space.description: Space where the stacks created by this deployment will be placed

stacks.description: List of stacks IDs created by the deployment

template_id.description: ID of the template this deployment belongs to

template_version_id.description: ID of the template version to deploy. Changing this will upgrade the deployment to the new version.

block.description: Input values for the template

checksum.description: SHA-256 checksum of the input value

id.description: Input identifier

secret.description: True if the input value is a secret

spacelift_template_version.description: `spacelift_template_version` represents a version of a Spacelift template. Each template can have multiple versions, each with its own state (DRAFT or PUBLISHED) and template body.

created_at.description: Unix timestamp when the template version was created

published_at.description: Unix timestamp when the template version was published

state.description: State of the template version. Value can be `DRAFT` or `PUBLISHED`.

template.description: Body of the template. Required if `state` is set to `PUBLISHED`.

template_id.description: ID of the template this version belongs to

ulid.description: Unique ULID of the template version

updated_at.description: Unix timestamp when the template version was last updated

spacelift_terraform_provider.description: `spacelift_terraform_provider` represents a Terraform provider in Spacelift's own provider registry.

description.description: Free-form description for human users, supports Markdown

public.description: Whether the provider is public or not, defaults to false (private)

space_id.description: ID (slug) of the space the provider is in

type.description: Type of the provider - should be unique in one account

spacelift_user.description:
`spacelift_user` represents a mapping between a Spacelift user (managed using an Identity Provider) and a Policy. A Policy defines what access rights the user has to a given Space.

Note: The `policy` attribute, previously used to assign roles to the user, is deprecated. Use the `spacelift_role_attachment` resource to manage user roles instead.

invitation_email.description: `invitation_email` will be used to send an invitation to the specified email address. This property is required when creating a new user. This property is optional when importing an existing user.

role.description: Type of access to the space. Possible values are: READ, WRITE, ADMIN

space_id.description: ID (slug) of the space the user has access to

spacelift_vcs_agent_pool.description: `spacelift_vcs_agent_pool` represents a Spacelift **VCS agent pool** - a logical group of proxies allowing Spacelift to access private VCS installations

config.description: VCS agent pool configuration, encoded using base64

description.description: Free-form VCS agent pool description for users

name.description: Name of the VCS agent pool, must be unique within an account

spacelift_version.description: `spacelift_version` allows to programmatically trigger a module version creation in response to arbitrary changes in the keepers section.

commit_sha.description: The commit SHA for which to trigger a version.

id.description: The ID of the triggered version.

keepers.description: Arbitrary map of values that, when changed, will trigger recreation of the resource.

module_id.description: ID of the module on which the version creation is to be triggered.

version_number.description: A semantic version number to set for the triggered version, example: 0.11.2

spacelift_webhook.description: `spacelift_webhook` represents a webhook endpoint to which Spacelift sends the POST request about run state changes.

enabled.description: enables or disables sending webhooks. Defaults to `true`.

endpoint.description: endpoint to send the POST request to

module_id.description: ID of the module which triggers the webhooks

retry_on_failure.description: whether to retry the webhook in case of failure. Defaults to `false`.

secret.description: secret used to sign each POST request so you're able to verify that the request comes from us. Defaults to an empty value. Note that once it's created, it will be just an empty string in the state due to security reasons.

secret_wo.description: `secret_wo` used to sign each POST request so you're able to verify that the request comes from us. Defaults to an empty value. The secret_wo is not stored in the state. Modify secret_wo_version to trigger an update. This field requires Terraform/OpenTofu 1.11+.

secret_wo_version.description: Used together with secret_wo to trigger an update to the secret. Increment this value when an update to secret_wo is required. This field requires Terraform/OpenTofu 1.11+.

stack_id.description: ID of the stack which triggers the webhooks

spacelift_worker_pool.description: `spacelift_worker_pool` represents a worker pool assigned to the Spacelift account.

config.description: credentials necessary to connect WorkerPool's workers to the control plane

csr.description: certificate signing request in base64. Changing this value will trigger a token reset.

drift_detection_run_limit.description: Limit of how many concurrent drift detection runs are allowed per worker pool

space_id.description: ID (slug) of the space the worker pool is in

spacelift_worker_pool_recycle.description: `spacelift_worker_pool_recycle` represents a worker pool recycle operation in Spacelift. This resource triggers a recycle of all workers in the specified worker pool, causing them to be replaced with fresh instances.

keepers.description: Arbitrary map of values that, when changed, will trigger recreation of the resource and thus a new worker pool recycle operation. This allows you to control when the worker pool recycle should happen.

worker_pool_id.description: ID of the worker pool to recycle

aws_account_id.description: the ID of the AWS account used by Spacelift for role assumption

spacelift_ai_integration.description: `spacelift_ai_integration` represents an integration with an AI/LLM provider.

ai_provider.description: AI provider backing the integration, one of `Anthropic`, `OpenAI`, `Google` or `Bedrock`

anthropic.description: Anthropic-specific configuration. Presence means this integration uses the Anthropic API.

bedrock.description: AWS Bedrock-specific configuration. Presence means this integration calls Bedrock through an AWS integration rather than using an API key.

enabled.description: Whether the integration can be used for LLM calls

google.description: Google-specific configuration. Presence means this integration uses the Gemini API.

is_spacelift_provided.description: Whether this is a read-only, Spacelift-managed integration shared with every account

models.description: Model identifiers this integration is pinned to, empty when it follows the default list for its provider. For Bedrock, its inference profiles.

openai.description: OpenAI-specific configuration. Presence means this integration uses the OpenAI API.

provider_integration_id.description: ID of the underlying provider integration, for example the AWS integration backing a Bedrock integration

space_id.description: ID of the space the integration belongs to, empty for Spacelift-provided integrations

spacelift_ai_integrations.description: `spacelift_ai_integrations` represents a list of all the AI integrations in the Spacelift account visible to the API user, including the read-only ones provided by Spacelift.

ai_provider.description: Only return the integrations backed by this AI provider, one of `Anthropic`, `Bedrock`, `Google` or `OpenAI`

spacelift_provided.description: Only return the integrations that are, or are not, provided by Spacelift. Leave unset to return both.

spacelift_aws_integration.description:
`spacelift_aws_integration` represents an integration with an AWS account. This integration is account-level and needs to be explicitly attached to individual stacks in order to take effect.

Note: when assuming credentials for **shared workers**, Spacelift will use `$accountName@$integrationID@$stackID@suffix` or `$accountName@$integrationID@$moduleID@$suffix` as [external ID](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_create_for-user_externalid.html) and `$runID@$stackID@$accountName` truncated to 64 characters as [session ID](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/STS/latest/APIReference/API_AssumeRole),$suffix will be `read` or `write`.

autoattach_enabled.description: Enables `autoattach:` labels functionality for this integration.

duration_seconds.description: Duration in seconds for which the assumed role credentials should be valid

external_id.description: Custom external ID (works only for private workers).

generate_credentials_in_worker.description: Generate AWS credentials in the private worker

integration_id.description: Immutable ID of the integration. Either `integration_id` or `name` must be specified.

name.description: Name of the AWS integration. Either `integration_id` or `name` must be specified.

region.description: AWS region to select a regional AWS STS endpoint.

role_arn.description: ARN of the AWS IAM role to attach

space_id.description: ID (slug) of the space the integration is in

tag_assume_role.description: When enabled, Spacelift will tag the assume role action with run and stack metadata.

spacelift_aws_integration_attachment.description: `spacelift_aws_integration_attachment` represents the attachment between a reusable AWS integration and a single stack or module.

attachment_id.description: Internal ID of the attachment entity

integration_id.description: ID of the integration to attach

module_id.description: ID of the module to attach the integration to

read.description: Indicates whether this attachment is used for read operations

stack_id.description: ID of the stack to attach the integration to

write.description: Indicates whether this attachment is used for write operations

spacelift_aws_integration_attachment_ext.description: `spacelift_aws_integration_attachment_external_id` is used to generate the external ID that would be used for role assumption when an AWS integration is attached to a stack or module.

assume_role_policy_statement.description: An assume role policy statement that can be attached to your role to allow Spacelift to assume it

external_id.description: The external ID that will be used during role assumption

integration_id.description: immutable ID (slug) of the AWS integration

module_id.description: immutable ID (slug) of the module

read.description: whether the integration will be used for read operations

stack_id.description: immutable ID (slug) of the stack

write.description: whether the integration will be used for write operations

spacelift_aws_integrations.description: `spacelift_aws_integrations` represents a list of all the AWS integrations in the Spacelift account visible to the API user.

spacelift_aws_role.description:
`spacelift_aws_role` represents [cross-account IAM role delegation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/tutorial_cross-account-with-roles.html) between the Spacelift worker and an individual stack or module. If this is set, Spacelift will use AWS STS to assume the supplied IAM role and put its temporary credentials in the runtime environment.

If you use private workers, you can also assume IAM role on the worker side using your own AWS credentials (e.g. from EC2 instance profile).

Note: when assuming credentials for **shared worker**, Spacelift will use `$accountName@$stackID` or `$accountName@$moduleID` as [external ID](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_create_for-user_externalid.html) and `$runID@$stackID@$accountName` truncated to 64 characters as [session ID](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/STS/latest/APIReference/API_AssumeRole).

duration_seconds.description: AWS IAM role session duration in seconds

external_id.description: Custom external ID (works only for private workers).

generate_credentials_in_worker.description: Generate AWS credentials in the private worker

module_id.description: ID of the module which assumes the AWS IAM role

region.description: AWS region to select a regional AWS STS endpoint.

role_arn.description: ARN of the AWS IAM role to attach

stack_id.description: ID of the stack which assumes the AWS IAM role

spacelift_azure_devops_integration.description: `spacelift_azure_devops_integration` returns details about Azure DevOps integration

id.description: Azure DevOps integration id. If not provided, the default integration will be returned

space_id.description: Azure DevOps integration space id

use_git_checkout.description: Indicates whether the integration should use git checkout. If false source code will be downloaded using the VCS API.

user_facing_host.description: Azure DevOps integration user facing host

vcs_checks.description: VCS checks configured for Azure DevOps repositories. Possible values: INDIVIDUAL, AGGREGATED, ALL. Defaults to INDIVIDUAL.

spacelift_azure_integration.description: `spacelift_azure_integration` represents an integration with an Azure AD tenant. This integration is account-level and needs to be explicitly attached to individual stacks in order to take effect. Note that you will need to provide admin consent manually for the integration to work

admin_consent_provided.description: Indicates whether admin consent has been performed for the AAD Application.

admin_consent_url.description: The URL to use to provide admin consent to the application in the customer's tenant

application_id.description: The applicationId of the Azure AD application used by the integration.

autoattach_enabled.description: Enables `autoattach:` labels functionality for this integration.

default_subscription_id.description: The default subscription ID to use, if one isn't specified at the stack/module level

display_name.description: The display name for the application in Azure. This is automatically generated when the integration is created, and cannot be changed without deleting and recreating the integration.

integration_id.description: Immutable ID of the integration. Either `integration_id` or `name` must be specified.

labels.description: Labels to set on the integration

name.description: The friendly name of the integration. Either `integration_id` or `name` must be specified.

object_id.description: The objectId of the Azure AD application used by the integration.

service_principal_object_id.description: This is the unique ID of the service principal object associated with this application. This ID can be useful when performing management operations against this application using programmatic interfaces.

space_id.description: ID (slug) of the space the integration is in

spacelift_azure_integration_attachment.description: `spacelift_azure_integration_attachment` represents the attachment between a reusable Azure integration and a single stack or module.

attachment_id.description: Internal ID of the attachment entity

integration_id.description: ID of the integration to attach

module_id.description: ID of the module to attach the integration to

read.description: Indicates whether this attachment is used for read operations

stack_id.description: ID of the stack to attach the integration to

subscription_id.description: Contains the Azure subscription ID to use with this Stack.  Overrides the default subscription ID set at the integration level.

write.description: Indicates whether this attachment is used for write operations

spacelift_azure_integrations.description: `spacelift_azure_integrations` represents a list of all the Azure integrations in the Spacelift account visible to the API user.

spacelift_bitbucket_cloud_integration.description: `spacelift_bitbucket_cloud_integration` returns details about Bitbucket Cloud integration

id.description: Bitbucket Cloud integration id. If not provided, the default integration will be returned

space_id.description: Bitbucket Cloud integration space id

vcs_checks.description: VCS checks configured for Bitbucket Cloud repositories. Possible values: INDIVIDUAL, AGGREGATED, ALL. Defaults to INDIVIDUAL.

spacelift_bitbucket_datacenter_integrati.description: `spacelift_bitbucket_datacenter_integration` returns details about Bitbucket Datacenter integration

id.description: Bitbucket Datacenter integration id. If not provided, the default integration will be returned

space_id.description: Bitbucket Datacenter integration space id

use_git_checkout.description: Indicates whether the integration should use git checkout. If false source code will be downloaded using the VCS API.

user_facing_host.description: Bitbucket Datacenter integration user facing host

username.description: Username which will be used to authenticate requests for cloning repositories

vcs_checks.description: VCS checks configured for Bitbucket Datacenter repositories. Possible values: INDIVIDUAL, AGGREGATED, ALL. Defaults to INDIVIDUAL.

spacelift_context.description: `spacelift_context` represents a Spacelift **context** - a collection of configuration elements (either environment variables or mounted files) that can be administratively attached to multiple stacks (`spacelift_stack`) or modules (`spacelift_module`) using a context attachment (`spacelift_context_attachment`)`

space_id.description: ID (slug) of the space the context is in

spacelift_context_attachment.description: `spacelift_context_attachment` represents a Spacelift attachment of a single context to a single stack or module, with a predefined priority.

module_id.description: ID of the attached module

priority.description: Priority of the context attachment. All the contexts attached to a stack are sorted by priority (lowest first), though values don't need to be unique. This ordering establishes precedence rules between contexts should there be a conflict and multiple contexts define the same value.

stack_id.description: ID of the attached stack

spacelift_contexts.description: `spacelift_contexts` represents all the contexts in the Spacelift account visible to the API user.

block.description: Require contexts to have one of the labels

spacelift_current_space.description: `spacelift_current_space` is a data source that provides information about the space that an administrative stack is in if the run is executed within Spacelift by a stack or module. This  makes it easier to create resources within the same space.

inherit_entities.description: indication whether access to this space inherits read access to entities from the parent space

labels.description: list of labels describing a space

spacelift_current_stack.description: `spacelift_current_stack` is a data source that provides information about the current administrative stack if the run is executed within Spacelift by a stack or module. This allows clever tricks like attaching contexts or policies to the stack that manages them.

spacelift_drift_detection.description: `spacelift_drift_detection` represents a Drift Detection configuration for a Stack. It will trigger a proposed run on the given schedule, which you can listen for using run state webhooks. If reconcile is true, then a tracked run will be triggered when drift is detected.

ignore_state.description: Controls whether drift detection should be performed on a stack in any final state instead of just 'Finished'.

reconcile.description: Whether a tracked run should be triggered when drift is detected.

schedule.description: List of cron schedule expressions based on which drift detection should be triggered.

stack_id.description: ID of the stack for which to set up drift detection

timezone.description: Timezone in which the schedule is expressed

spacelift_environment_variable.description: `spacelift_environment_variable` defines an environment variable on the context (`spacelift_context`), stack (`spacelift_stack`) or a module (`spacelift_module`), thereby allowing to pass and share various secrets and configuration with Spacelift stacks.

context_id.description: ID of the context on which the environment variable is defined

module_id.description: ID of the module on which the environment variable is defined

stack_id.description: ID of the stack on which the environment variable is defined

write_only.description: indicates whether the value can be read back outside a Run

spacelift_gcp_service_account.description: `spacelift_gcp_service_account` represents a Google Cloud Platform service account that's linked to a particular Stack or Module. These accounts are created by Spacelift on per-stack basis, and can be added as members to as many organizations and projects as needed. During a Run or a Task, temporary credentials for those service accounts are injected into the environment, which allows credential-less GCP Terraform provider setup.

module_id.description: ID of the stack which uses GCP service account credentials

service_account_email.description: email address of the GCP service account dedicated for this stack

stack_id.description: ID of the stack which uses GCP service account credentials

spacelift_github_enterprise_integration.description: `spacelift_github_enterprise_integration` returns details about Github Enterprise integration

id.description: Github integration id. If not provided, the default integration will be returned

space_id.description: Github integration space id

use_git_checkout.description: Indicates whether the integration should use git checkout. If false source code will be downloaded using the VCS API.

vcs_checks.description: VCS checks configured for Github repositories. Possible values: INDIVIDUAL, AGGREGATED, ALL. Defaults to INDIVIDUAL.

id.description: Gitlab integration id. If not provided, the default integration will be returned

space_id.description: Gitlab integration space id

use_git_checkout.description: Indicates whether the integration should use git checkout. If false source code will be downloaded using the VCS API.

vcs_checks.description: VCS checks configured for GitLab repositories. Possible values: INDIVIDUAL, AGGREGATED, ALL. Defaults to INDIVIDUAL.

spacelift_gitlab_webhook_endpoint.description: `spacelift_gitlab_webhook_endpoint` returns details about Gitlab webhook endpoint

spacelift_idp_group_mapping.description: `spacelift_idp_group_mapping` represents a data source for retrieving information about an existing IdP group mapping in Spacelift.

description.description: Description of the IdP group mapping

name.description: Name of the IdP group as defined in the SSO provider

policy.description: List of access rules for the IdP group.

spacelift_ips.description: `spacelift_ips` returns the list of Spacelift's outgoing IP addresses, which you can use to whitelist connections coming from the Spacelift's "mothership". **NOTE:** this does not include the IP addresses of the workers in Spacelift's public worker pool. If you need to ensure that requests made during runs originate from a known set of IP addresses, please consider setting up a [private worker pool](https://docs.spacelift.io/concepts/worker-pools).

cidrs.description: list of Spacelift IP addresses in CIDR notation (/32) for easy use in security group rules

ips.description: the list of spacelift.io outgoing IP addresses

spacelift_module.description: `spacelift_module` is a special type of a stack used to test and version Terraform modules.

administrative.description: indicates whether this module can administer others

aws_assume_role_policy_statement.description: AWS IAM assume role policy statement setting up trust relationship

branch.description: GitHub branch to apply changes to

description.description: free-form module description for human users (supports Markdown)

enable_local_preview.description: Indicates whether local preview versions can be triggered on this Module.

git_sparse_checkout_paths.description: Git sparse checkout paths is an optional list of paths to use for sparse checkout. If not set, the entire repository will be checked out.

module_id.description: ID (slug) of the module

name.description: The module name will by default be inferred from the repository name if it follows the terraform-provider-name naming convention. However, if the repository doesn't follow this convention, or you want to give it a custom name, you can provide it here.

origin.description: Set when the source uses the installed account-level Origin integration.

project_root.description: Project root is the optional directory relative to the repository root containing the module source code.

protect_from_deletion.description: Protect this module from accidental deletion. If set, attempts to delete this module will fail.

raw_git.description: One-way VCS integration using a raw Git repository link

repository.description: Name of the repository, without the owner part

runner_image.description: Name of the Docker image used to process Runs

shared_accounts.description: List of the accounts (subdomains) which should have access to the Module

space_id.description: ID (slug) of the space the module is in

space_shares.description: List of the space IDs which should have access to the Module

spacelift_repo.description: Set when the source is a Spacelift repo, whose ID (slug) is `repository`

terraform_provider.description: The module provider will by default be inferred from the repository name if it follows the terraform-provider-name naming convention. However, if the repository doesn't follow this convention, or you gave the module a custom name, you can provide the provider name here.

worker_pool_id.description: ID of the worker pool to use

workflow_tool.description: Defines the tool that will be used to execute the workflow. This can be one of `OPEN_TOFU`, `TERRAFORM_FOSS` or `CUSTOM`.

spacelift_modules.description: `spacelift_modules` represents all the modules in the Spacelift account visible to the API user, matching predicates.

modules.description: List of modules matching the predicates

block.description: Require modules to be administrative or not
Require modules to be on one of the branches
Require modules to be on one of the commits
Require modules to have one of the labels
Require modules to have one of the names
Require modules to be in one of the project roots
Require modules to be in one of the repositories
Require modules to use one of the worker pools

spacelift_mounted_file.description: `spacelift_mounted_file` represents a file mounted in each Run's workspace that is part of a configuration of a context (`spacelift_context`), stack (`spacelift_stack`) or a module (`spacelift_module`). In principle, it's very similar to an environment variable (`spacelift_environment_variable`) except that the value is written to the filesystem rather than passed to the environment.

content.description: content of the mounted file encoded using Base-64

context_id.description: ID of the context where the mounted file is stored

module_id.description: ID of the module where the mounted file is stored

relative_path.description: relative path to the mounted file

stack_id.description: ID of the stack where the mounted file is stored

write_only.description: indicates whether the value can be read back outside a Run

spacelift_named_webhook.description: `spacelift_named_webhook` represents a named webhook endpoint used for creating webhookswhich are referred to in Notification policies to route messages.

endpoint.description: endpoint to send the requests to

labels.description: labels for the webhook to use when referring in policies or filtering them

name.description: the name for the webhook which will also be used to generate the id

retry_on_failure.description: whether to retry the webhook in case of failure

secret_header_keys.description: secret header keys which are currently set for this webhook

space_id.description: ID of the space the webhook is in

spacelift_plugin.description: `spacelift_plugin` represents a Spacelift **plugin** - an instance of a plugin template that can be used to extend Spacelift functionality.

space_id.description: ID of the space the plugin is in

stack_label.description: Label used when attaching the plugin to stacks

spacelift_plugin_template.description: `spacelift_plugin_template` represents a Spacelift **plugin template** - a reusable template that defines a plugin's behavior and can be instantiated multiple times as plugins.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the plugin template was created

is_global.description: Whether this is a global (Spacelift-provided) plugin template

labels.description: Labels applied to the plugin template

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the plugin template was last updated

spacelift_policies.description: `spacelift_policies` can find all policies that have certain labels.

spacelift_policy.description: `spacelift_policy` represents a Spacelift **policy** - a collection of customer-defined rules that are applied by Spacelift at one of the decision points within the application.

engine_type.description: type of engine used to evaluate the policy

space_id.description: ID (slug) of the space the policy is in

spacelift_repo.description: `spacelift_repo` returns details about a Spacelift repo, the built-in VCS provider storing source code directly in Spacelift.

created_at.description: Unix timestamp of when the repo was created

space_id.description: ID (slug) of the space the repo is in

stacks.description: IDs (slugs) of the stacks using this repo as their source code provider

updated_at.description: Unix timestamp of when the repo was last updated

vcs_checks.description: VCS checks configured for the repo. One of `INDIVIDUAL`, `AGGREGATED` or `ALL`.

spacelift_repos.description: `spacelift_repos` returns the Spacelift repos in a single space. Repos are not inherited by child spaces, so only repos created directly in the given space are returned.

repos.description: List of repos in the space

space_id.description: ID (slug) of the space to list repos from

spacelift_role.description:
`spacelift_role` represents a Spacelift **role** - a collection of permissions that can be assigned to IdP groups or API keys to control access to Spacelift resources and operations.

You can either filter roles by their unique identifier (`role_id`) or by their URL-friendly unique identifier (`slug`).

**Note:** you must have admin access to the `root` Space in order to retrieve roles.

actions.description: List of actions (permissions) associated with the role

description.description: Human-readable, free-form description of the role

is_system.description: Whether the role is a system role. System roles are built-in roles with predefined permissions for specific Spacelift functionality and cannot be modified or deleted.

name.description: Human-readable, free-form name of the role. Can be used to filter roles.

role_id.description: Unique identifier (ULID) of the role. Can be used to filter roles. Example: `01K07523Q8B4TBF0YHQRF6J5MW`.

slug.description: URL-friendly unique identifier of the role, generated from the name. Example: `space-admin`.

spacelift_role_actions.description: The `spacelift_role_actions` data source provides a list of all valid actions that can be assigned to roles in Spacelift.

actions.description: List of all valid actions that can be assigned to roles in Spacelift.

created_by.description: Login of the user who created the saved filter

data.description: Data is the JSON representation of the filter data

id.description: Globally unique ID of the saved filter

is_public.description: Toggle whether the filter is public or not

type.description: Type describes the type of the filter. It is used to determine which view the filter is for

spacelift_saved_filters.description: `spacelift_saved_filters` can find all saved filters that have certain type or name

spacelift_scheduled_delete_stack.description: `spacelift_scheduled_delete_stack` represents a scheduling configuration for a Stack. It will trigger a stack deletion task at the given timestamp.

at.description: Timestamp (unix timestamp) at which time the scheduling should happen.

delete_resources.description: Indicates whether the resources of the stack should be deleted.

stack_id.description: Stack ID of the scheduling config

spacelift_scheduled_run.description: `spacelift_scheduled_run` represents a scheduling configuration for a Stack. It will trigger a run on the given timestamp/schedule.

at.description: Timestamp (unix timestamp) at which time the scheduled run should happen.

every.description: List of cron schedule expressions based on which the scheduled run should be triggered.

next_schedule.description: Timestamp (unix timestamp) of when the next run will be scheduled.

stack_id.description: Stack ID of the scheduling config

timezone.description: Timezone in which the schedule is expressed. Defaults to `UTC`.

block.description: Customer provided runtime configuration for this scheduled run.

project_root.description: Project root is the optional directory relative to the workspace root containing the entrypoint to the Stack.

runner_image.description: Name of the Docker image used to process Runs

terraform_workflow_tool.description: Defines the tool that will be used to execute the workflow. This can be one of `OPEN_TOFU`, `TERRAFORM_FOSS` or `CUSTOM`. Defaults to `TERRAFORM_FOSS`.

block.description: Environment variables for the run

spacelift_scheduled_task.description: `spacelift_scheduled_task` represents a scheduling configuration for a Stack. It will trigger a task on the given timestamp/schedule.

at.description: Timestamp (unix timestamp) at which time the scheduling should happen.

every.description: List of cron schedule expressions based on which the scheduled task should be triggered.

stack_id.description: Stack ID of the scheduled task

timezone.description: Timezone in which the schedule is expressed. Defaults to `UTC`.

spacelift_space.description: `spacelift_space` represents a Spacelift **space** - a collection of resources such as stacks, modules, policies, etc. Allows for more granular access control. Can have a parent space.

inherit_entities.description: indication whether access to this space inherits read access to entities from the parent space

labels.description: list of labels describing a space

space_id.description: immutable ID (slug) of the space

spacelift_space_by_path.description:
`spacelift_space_by_path` represents a Spacelift **space** - a collection of resources such as stacks, modules, policies, etc. Allows for more granular access control. Can have a parent space. In contrary to `spacelift_space`, this resource is identified by a path, not by an ID. For this data source to work, path must be unique. If there are multiple spaces with the same path, this datasource will fail. 
This data source can be used either with absolute paths (starting with root) or relative paths. When using a relative path, the path is relative to the current run's space. 
**Disclaimer:** 
This datasource can only be used in a stack that resides in a space with inheritance enabled. In addition, the parent spaces (excluding root) must also have inheritance enabled.

labels.description: list of labels describing a space

space_path.description: path to the space - a series of space names separated by `/`

spacelift_spaces.description: `spacelift_spaces` can find all spaces in the spacelift organization.

additional_project_globs.description: Project globs is an optional list of paths to track changes of in addition to the project root.

manage_state.description: Determines if Spacelift should manage state for this stack

opentofu.description: OpenTofu-specific configuration. Presence means this Stack is a native OpenTofu Stack.

project_root.description: Project root is the optional directory relative to the workspace root containing the entrypoint to the Stack.

protect_from_deletion.description: Protect this stack from accidental deletion. If set, attempts to delete this stack will fail.

pulumi.description: Pulumi-specific configuration. Presence means this Stack is a Pulumi Stack.

raw_git.description: One-way VCS integration using a raw Git repository link

repository.description: Name of the repository, without the owner part

runner_image.description: Name of the Docker image used to process Runs

space_id.description: ID (slug) of the space the stack is in

spacelift_repo.description: Set when the source is a Spacelift repo, whose ID (slug) is `repository`

stack_id.description: ID (slug) of the stack

terraform_external_state_access.description: Indicates whether you can access the Stack state file from other stacks or outside of Spacelift.

terraform_smart_sanitization.description: Indicates whether runs on this will use terraform's sensitive value system to sanitize the outputs of Terraform state and plans in spacelift instead of sanitizing all fields.

terraform_workflow_tool.description: Defines the tool that will be used to execute the workflow. This can be one of `OPEN_TOFU`, `TERRAFORM_FOSS` or `CUSTOM`.

terragrunt.description: Terragrunt-specific configuration. Presence means this Stack is a Terragrunt Stack.

spacelift_stack_aws_role.description:
~> **Note:** `spacelift_stack_aws_role` is deprecated. Please use `spacelift_aws_role` instead. The functionality is identical.

`spacelift_stack_aws_role` represents [cross-account IAM role delegation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/tutorial_cross-account-with-roles.html) between the Spacelift worker and an individual stack or module. If this is set, Spacelift will use AWS STS to assume the supplied IAM role and put its temporary credentials in the runtime environment.

If you use private workers, you can also assume IAM role on the worker side using your own AWS credentials (e.g. from EC2 instance profile).

Note: when assuming credentials for **shared worker**, Spacelift will use `$accountName@$stackID` or `$accountName@$moduleID` as [external ID](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_create_for-user_externalid.html) and `$runID@$stackID@$accountName` truncated to 64 characters as [session ID](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/STS/latest/APIReference/API_AssumeRole).

duration_seconds.description: AWS IAM role session duration in seconds

external_id.description: Custom external ID (works only for private workers).

generate_credentials_in_worker.description: Generate AWS credentials in the private worker

module_id.description: ID of the module which assumes the AWS IAM role

region.description: AWS region to select a regional AWS STS endpoint.

role_arn.description: ARN of the AWS IAM role to attach

stack_id.description: ID of the stack which assumes the AWS IAM role

spacelift_stack_gcp_service_account.description:
~> **Note:** `spacelift_stack_gcp_service_account` is deprecated. Please use `spacelift_gcp_service_account` instead. The functionality is identical.

`spacelift_stack_gcp_service_account` represents a Google Cloud Platform service account that's linked to a particular Stack or Module. These accounts are created by Spacelift on per-stack basis, and can be added as members to as many organizations and projects as needed. During a Run or a Task, temporary credentials for those service accounts are injected into the environment, which allows credential-less GCP Terraform provider setup.

module_id.description: ID of the stack which uses GCP service account credentials

service_account_email.description: email address of the GCP service account dedicated for this stack

stack_id.description: ID of the stack which uses GCP service account credentials

spacelift_template.description: `spacelift_template` represents a Spacelift template (versioned blueprint), which is a collection of blueprint versions that can be used to create stacks.

created_at.description: Unix timestamp when the template was created

space.description: ID of the space the template is in

updated_at.description: Unix timestamp when the template was last updated

spacelift_template_deployment.description: `spacelift_template_deployment` represents an existing deployment of a Spacelift template.

created_at.description: Unix timestamp when the deployment was created

space.description: Space where the stacks created by this deployment are placed

stacks.description: List of stacks IDs created by the deployment

template_id.description: ID of the template this deployment belongs to

template_version_id.description: ID of the template version used by this deployment

spacelift_template_version.description: `spacelift_template_version` represents a version of a Spacelift template. Each template can have multiple versions, each with its own state (DRAFT or PUBLISHED) and template body. A version can be looked up by its ID (slug) using `version_id` or by its version number using `version_number`. Exactly one of `version_id` or `version_number` must be provided.

created_at.description: Unix timestamp when the template version was created

published_at.description: Unix timestamp when the template version was published

state.description: State of the template version. Value can be `DRAFT` or `PUBLISHED`.

template_id.description: ID of the template this version belongs to

ulid.description: Unique ULID of the template version

updated_at.description: Unix timestamp when the template version was last updated

version_id.description: ID (slug) of the template version. Conflicts with `version_number`.

spacelift_tool_versions.description: Lists supported versions for a given tool.

tool.description: The tool to get a list of supported versions for. This can be one of `KUBECTL`, `OPEN_TOFU`, `TERRAFORM_FOSS`, or `TERRAGRUNT`.

versions.description: Supported versions of the given tool.

spacelift_user.description: `spacelift_user` represents a data source for retrieving information about an existing Spacelift user. This allows you to reference user information in your Terraform configurations.

invitation_email.description: Email address used for the user invitation

policy.description: List of policies (space access rules) assigned to the user

spacelift_vcs_agent_pool.description: `spacelift_vcs_agent_pool` represents a Spacelift **VCS agent pool** - a logical group of proxies allowing Spacelift to access private VCS installations

description.description: Free-form VCS agent pool description for users

name.description: Name of the VCS agent pool

vcs_agent_pool_id.description: ID of the VCS agent pool to retrieve

spacelift_vcs_agent_pools.description: `spacelift_vcs_agent_pools` represents the VCS agent pools assigned to the Spacelift account.

spacelift_webhook.description: `spacelift_webhook` represents a webhook endpoint to which Spacelift sends the POST request about run state changes.

endpoint.description: endpoint to send the POST request to

module_id.description: ID of the stack which triggers the webhooks

retry_on_failure.description: whether to retry the webhook in case of failure

stack_id.description: ID of the stack which triggers the webhooks

spacelift_worker_pool.description: `spacelift_worker_pool` represents a worker pool assigned to the Spacelift account.

config.description: credentials necessary to connect WorkerPool's workers to the control plane

drift_detection_run_limit.description: Limit of how many concurrent drift detection runs are allowed per worker pool

space_id.description: ID (slug) of the space the worker pool is in

spacelift_worker_pools.description: `spacelift_worker_pools` represents the worker pools assigned to the Spacelift account.
